emb:L2014483023.clinical_problem: community-acquired pneumonia pathogen classification (viral vs bacterial vs mycoplasma)
emb:L2014483023.patient_population: 1,769 children with community-acquired pneumonia, grouped by causative pathogen (virus, bacteria, mycoplasma)
emb:L2014483023.model_description: The model takes chest X-rays from children with community-acquired pneumonia and classifies either the whole-lung image or a lesion region-of-interest to predict the likely causative pathogen (virus, bacteria, or mycoplasma pneumoniae). It was trained and tested on a 7:1:2 split of 1,769 pneumonia cases using a convolutional neural network, comparing a full-lung model against a model restricted to the lesion area. It is intended to help distinguish pathogen type from chest radiograph appearance alone.
emb:L2014483023.headline_result: Full lung model AUC 0.798 and local model AUC 0.819 for mycoplasma pneumonia (best-performing category); overall accuracy 61.85% (full lung) and 58.04%/63.77%/54.05% variants across models

emb:L2014452480.model_family: ensemble of deep convolutional neural networks
emb:L2014452480.clinical_problem: quantification of neonatal lung disease / bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) severity
emb:L2014452480.patient_population: premature infants near term (n=107), imaged with quiet-breathing MRI, with and without bronchopulmonary dysplasia
emb:L2014452480.model_description: The model segments premature infant lungs on quiet-breathing MRI using an ensemble of deep convolutional neural networks, then reconstructs a 3D lung model and derives descriptors of volume, shape, surface, and signal intensity. It was trained and validated in 107 near-term premature infants against manual annotation, reaching a volumetric Dice score of 0.908 (0.880 in an independent validation cohort). The resulting MRI-derived lung descriptors were used to separate infants with and without bronchopulmonary dysplasia and to grade BPD severity, without radiation exposure.
emb:L2014452480.release_evidence: preprint (medRxiv); no repository or product mentioned
emb:L2014452480.headline_result: Volumetric Dice score 0.908 (independent cohort 0.880); AUC 0.92 for BPD vs no BPD, AUC 0.84 mild vs severe BPD, AUC 0.75 for severity prediction

emb:L2012930154.model_description: This review describes assistance systems used in prenatal ultrasound, from simple reference curves to newer systems built on artificial intelligence. It argues that AI-based assistance has the potential to change how sonographic fetal examinations are performed, improving efficacy, efficiency, and quality of the exam, though no specific model or trial is described.

emb:L2012991291.model_family: 3D mixed-scale asymmetric convolutional segmentation network, applied to five canonical CNN backbones
emb:L2012991291.clinical_problem: infant brain tissue segmentation (gray matter, white matter, cerebrospinal fluid) for study of early brain development
emb:L2012991291.patient_population: 23 six-month-old infants (iSeg-2019 dataset), T1- and T2-weighted brain MRI
emb:L2012991291.model_description: 3D-MASNet replaces the standard convolutional layer in existing brain-segmentation networks with a mixed-scale block of asymmetric convolution kernels during training, then equivalently converts it back to the original network architecture for inference. Applied to T1- and T2-weighted MRI from 23 six-month-old infants, it segments the brain into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid, improving five existing CNN segmentation models and ranking first among 30 teams on the iSeg-2019 Grand Challenge validation set.
emb:L2012991291.release_evidence: preprint (bioRxiv); no repository or product mentioned
emb:L2012991291.headline_result: Dice coefficient 0.931 (GM), 0.912 (WM), 0.961 (CSF); ranked first among 30 teams on iSeg-2019 Grand Challenge validation set

emb:L2010386034.clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease by fetal echocardiography
emb:L2010386034.patient_population: fetuses undergoing fetal echocardiography for congenital heart disease screening
emb:L2010386034.model_description: This review discusses potential uses of artificial intelligence in fetal cardiology, including improving prenatal detection rates of congenital heart disease on fetal echocardiography, providing more individualized prognosis, and automatically quantifying cardiac function metrics. It notes most existing evidence is retrospective, with few prospective trials, and raises ethical and governance concerns that must be addressed before wider adoption.

emb:L2011987687.exclusion_reason: non-imaging clinical prediction model (NHANES demographic, laboratory and clinical predictors, not image-based)

emb:L635519576.exclusion_reason: basic neuroscience fMRI research on cognition, not a diagnostic AI model applied to radiology

emb:L634713122.clinical_problem: diagnosis of WHO-defined primary endpoint pneumonia on chest X-ray in children under 5
emb:L634713122.patient_population: children under 5 years old in Bangladesh with suspected pneumonia; approximately 10,000 chest X-rays from a WHO-supported surveillance study
emb:L634713122.model_description: This is a study protocol describing plans to build a deep-learning tool for diagnosing paediatric pneumonia on chest X-ray. Approximately 10,000 images from children under 5 in Bangladesh will be labeled by trained clinicians/radiologists for the presence of WHO-defined primary endpoint pneumonia in each lung (with a third reader for disagreement), and convolutional neural networks will be used to segment and align the lungs before classifying images for pneumonia. No results are reported since this is a protocol.
emb:L634713122.release_evidence: "All X-ray labels and statistical code will be made openly available. The model and images will be made available on request."

emb:L2014436239.exclusion_reason: adult breast cancer screening context, no pediatric population

emb:L2011991332.clinical_problem: estimation of fetal weight (EFW) for evaluating fetal growth and pregnancy outcome
emb:L2011991332.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound (and some 3D ultrasound/MRI) weight estimation
emb:L2011991332.model_description: This review summarizes methods for estimating fetal weight from maternal and fetal ultrasound parameters, from traditional formulas (e.g., Hadlock) to 3D ultrasound and MRI volumetric measurement, and notes that a big-data neural-network-based prediction model shows a better coincidence rate than traditional ultrasonic estimation. No specific model, dataset, or performance metric is given.

emb:L2011157480.exclusion_reason: dental imaging (panoramic radiograph age estimation), excluded modality

emb:L2014449305.exclusion_reason: basic neuroscience research predicting cognition and socio-demographic factors from MRI, not a clinical radiology diagnostic task

emb:L635442190.model_family: Mask R-CNN with ElliFit ellipse fitting
emb:L635442190.clinical_problem: prenatal ultrasound measurement of fetal head circumference
emb:L635442190.patient_population: 190 ultrasound images of fetal head (test set)
emb:L635442190.model_description: The model segments the fetal head on 2D ultrasound images using Mask R-CNN, fits an ellipse to the segmentation mask with the ElliFit algorithm, and computes head circumference using the Ramanujan formula. A custom loss function tying the measurement error into training was used to improve accuracy and speed. On 190 test images it reached a Dice coefficient of 96.89% and a measurement error of 0.33 mm, processing each image in 0.33 seconds.
emb:L635442190.headline_result: Dice coefficient 96.89%±1.01%; head circumference measurement error 0.33±1.54 mm; 0.33 s per image

emb:L2011476111.model_family: deep learning (TW3-C-RUS based bone age assessment system)
emb:L2011476111.clinical_problem: bone age assessment to assist junior pediatric radiologists
emb:L2011476111.model_description: A deep-learning bone-age assessment (BAA) system evaluates metacarpal and phalangeal maturity on hand-wrist radiographs using the TW3-C-RUS standard. It was compared against a junior pediatric radiologist reading alone and the same radiologist assisted by the system, referenced against a senior radiologist's assessment aided by BAA. With BAA assistance, the junior radiologist's error and reading time both improved.
emb:L2011476111.headline_result: System RMSE 0.62 years, MAE 0.47 years; with BAA assistance junior radiologist RMSE improved from 0.71 to 0.27 years and MAE from 0.90 to 0.38 years; mean reading time shortened from 4 min 40 s to 2 min 15 s

emb:L2011202886.exclusion_reason: broad review of AI across pediatric surgery (imaging, pathology, robotics, rehabilitation), not focused on radiology imaging

emb:L2006896749.exclusion_reason: exploratory ultrasound image-analysis study characterizing splenic echogenicity, not a diagnostic AI/ML application

emb:L2010755210.exclusion_reason: histopathology image analysis (immunostained tissue sections), not radiologic imaging

emb:L2012383149.exclusion_reason: prediction model uses first-trimester screening test values (serum markers, NT measurement) as structured inputs, not image-based analysis

emb:L2013097559.model_family: XGBoost, SVM, and Random Forest classifiers
emb:L2013097559.clinical_problem: detection of epilepsy from brain imaging
emb:L2013097559.patient_population: 63 patients with epilepsy and 259 healthy controls; preoperative resting-state functional MRI
emb:L2013097559.model_description: The model uses features derived from resting-state functional MRI hemodynamic 'latency' maps (via principal component analysis of latency z-scores across 36 brain seed regions) as inputs to machine-learning classifiers (XGBoost, SVM, Random Forest) to distinguish patients with epilepsy from healthy controls. It was trained and tested on preoperative rs-fMRI from 63 epilepsy patients and 259 controls, intended as an adjunctive diagnostic tool for pediatric epilepsy.
emb:L2013097559.dataset_size: 63 patients with epilepsy and 259 healthy controls
emb:L2013097559.headline_result: Best model (XGBoost) test AUC 0.79, accuracy 74%, specificity 73%, sensitivity 77%

emb:L2013328146.exclusion_reason: theoretical review of dissociative identity disorder neurobiology, no AI/ML model

emb:L2013805678.exclusion_reason: neural network uses clinical and laboratory parameters (BMI, bilirubin, coagulation time, amniotic fluid index), not image-based analysis

emb:L2014180410.model_family: previously reported AI bone-age system (deep learning-based, implementing TW3 and TW-China05 methods)
emb:L2014180410.clinical_problem: bone age assessment method comparison in Tibetan children
emb:L2014180410.patient_population: 305 Tibetan children (209 boys, 96 girls) aged 4-18 years, left-hand radiographs
emb:L2014180410.model_description: A previously reported AI bone-age system was used to apply the TW3 (RUS and Carpal) and TW-China05 methods to left-hand radiographs, and its results were compared against manual Greulich-Pyle assessment by two experienced reviewers in 305 Tibetan children aged 4-18. The Greulich-Pyle atlas correlated most strongly with chronological age (r=0.961) among the methods tested, with the AI-implemented TW3-RUS method second (r=0.941).
emb:L2014180410.dataset_size: 305 Tibetan children (209 boys, 96 girls), aged 4-18 years
emb:L2014180410.headline_result: Correlation with chronological age: GP atlas r=0.961, TW3-RUS r=0.941, TW-China05 r=0.937, TW3-Carpal r=0.895

emb:L2015747953.patient_population: 12,611 hand X-ray images from the RSNA Bone Age database
emb:L2015747953.model_description: Two pretrained deep neural network architectures (Inception-ResNet-V2 and Xception) were compared for estimating skeletal (bone) age from hand X-rays using the public RSNA Bone Age dataset of 12,611 images. Both networks output a predicted bone age from the radiograph, achieving similarly high correlation with reference age (R-squared 0.935 and 0.942, respectively) even with limited training instances.
emb:L2015747953.dataset_size: 12,611 hand X-ray images (RSNA Bone Age database)

emb:L634106700.model_family: HOG/LBP/SIFT feature extraction with SVM and k-nearest neighbor classifiers
emb:L634106700.clinical_problem: automated bone age assessment for growth disorder screening
emb:L634106700.patient_population: Iranian children's hand radiographs (test set); University of Southern California hand atlas (training set)
emb:L634106700.model_description: A computer-aided diagnosis system extracts hand-wrist carpal and epiphyseal region features (HOG, LBP, dense SIFT) and classifies bone-age stage using a support vector machine, trained on the University of Southern California hand atlas and tested on Iranian children's radiographs. It reached substantial agreement with an experienced radiologist's bone-age reading, with better accuracy in female than male radiographs.
emb:L634106700.dataset_size: Iranian children's radiographs (test set); USC hand atlas (training set)
emb:L634106700.headline_result: Accuracy 90% (female), 71.42% (male); MAE 0.16 years (female), 0.42 years (male); Cohen's kappa 0.86 (female), 0.6 (male)
emb:L634106700.study_design: retrospective external validation diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L634404555.exclusion_reason: general/adult brain tumor MRI classification study; pediatric mentioned only incidentally, no pediatric-specific population or data given

emb:L2010333989.model_family: conjunctive clause evolutionary algorithm (CCEA) for feature selection; k-nearest neighbors classifier
emb:L2010333989.clinical_problem: autism spectrum disorder diagnosis using neuroimaging and behavioral features
emb:L2010333989.patient_population: 28 children aged 7-14 years, with and without autism spectrum disorder
emb:L2010333989.model_description: The model combines structural brain MRI measurements (regional volume, area, cortical thickness, mean curvature) with behavioral features to identify children with autism spectrum disorder. A novel evolutionary algorithm (CCEA) selects the most discriminating features from a small sample of 28 children aged 7-14, and a separate k-nearest-neighbors classifier validates the selected features for ASD prediction.
emb:L2010333989.release_evidence: preprint (medRxiv); no repository or product mentioned

emb:L2006794605.model_family: fully convolutional neural network (FCNN) with regression branch and attention mechanism
emb:L2006794605.clinical_problem: automated measurement of fetal head circumference, biparietal diameter, and occipitofrontal diameter
emb:L2006794605.patient_population: HC18 public fetal head ultrasound dataset
emb:L2006794605.model_description: An end-to-end fully convolutional network segments the fetal head on 2D ultrasound images while a parallel regression branch predicts biparietal diameter (BPD) and occipitofrontal diameter (OFD); head circumference is then derived from the segmentation. The network uses a feature pyramid with an attention mechanism and a region-of-interest pooling layer tailored to the elliptical head shape, trained and evaluated on the public HC18 dataset, and is reported to outperform existing fetal head measurement methods.
emb:L2006794605.dataset_size: HC18 public dataset (fetal head ultrasound images)

emb:L2009014992.exclusion_reason: predicts general cognitive ability from task-based fMRI as a neuroscience research question, not a clinical radiology diagnostic task

emb:L2007965533.exclusion_reason: neuropsychological testing study, no imaging or AI/ML model

emb:L2001875905.clinical_problem: segmentation of the hippocampus in infant brain MRI to study early brain development
emb:L2001875905.patient_population: infants imaged longitudinally with T1-weighted brain MRI at 2 weeks and 3, 6, 9, and 12 months of age
emb:L2001875905.model_description: A longitudinal classification-regression random forest model segments the hippocampus on infant T1-weighted brain MRI at each timepoint, using information from the prior timepoint's segmentation together with the current scan's appearance. It was evaluated on infants scanned at 2 weeks and 3, 6, 9, and 12 months of age, and is reported to outperform existing classification/regression forest methods for this task.

emb:L2008484440.exclusion_reason: correlational rs-fMRI connectivity analysis of fatigue in perinatal stroke, not a diagnostic AI/ML model

emb:L2003661396.body_region: fetal (nasal bone, nuchal region, limbs, heart)
emb:L2003661396.clinical_problem: prenatal ultrasound detection of Down syndrome
emb:L2003661396.patient_population: fetuses undergoing first- and second-trimester ultrasound screening (11-22 weeks)
emb:L2003661396.model_description: This review surveys ultrasound imaging features used to screen for Down syndrome in the first (11-14 weeks) and second (15-22 weeks) trimesters, such as nasal bone hypoplasia/absence, nuchal thickness, fetal heart rate, and limb-bone shortening, and introduces the use of deep-learning techniques for identifying these features, without presenting a specific model or its performance.

emb:L2003665244.model_family: two-stage fully convolutional network (shallow FCN + multi-scale FCN)
emb:L2003665244.clinical_problem: automatic extraction (segmentation) of the fetal brain for downstream MRI analysis
emb:L2003665244.model_description: A two-step deep-learning pipeline first uses a shallow fully convolutional network to rapidly locate and crop a region of interest around the fetal brain on 2D in-utero MRI slices, then refines the segmentation with a deeper multi-scale FCN using dilated convolutions and residual learning to produce the final brain mask. Evaluated on 88 fetal MRI scans, it located the fetal brain with 100% accuracy and processed one MRI stack in about 6 seconds.
emb:L2003665244.headline_result: Brain localization accuracy 100%; Dice score 0.958, sensitivity 0.950, precision 0.968; ~6 seconds per MRI stack

emb:L627536652.model_family: self-organizing map deep convolutional neural network (SOM-DCNN) with sparse autoencoder
emb:L627536652.clinical_problem: segmentation and tissue classification of the neonatal brain on MRI
emb:L627536652.model_description: An atlas-free scheme segments and classifies neonatal brain MRI tissue using a hybrid self-organizing-map deep convolutional neural network combined with a sparse autoencoder for classification, intended to avoid the atlas-dependence and manual interaction that limit prior infant brain segmentation methods. Performance is reported using the Dice metric and said to be more accurate than existing segmentation schemes, though exact numeric results are not given in the abstract.

emb:L2005004652.model_family: cascade forest (gcForest) classifier with cuckoo-search-based feature selection
emb:L2005004652.clinical_problem: diagnosis of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) from functional brain imaging
emb:L2005004652.patient_population: ADHD-200 public dataset (children with and without ADHD)
emb:L2005004652.model_description: MCS-CF preprocesses resting-state functional MRI, extracts functional-connectivity and amplitude-of-low-frequency-fluctuation features, and uses a Modified Cuckoo Search algorithm to select the most useful features before classifying subjects as ADHD or control with a cascade-forest (gcForest) classifier. It was evaluated on the public ADHD-200 dataset and reported using accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, intended to improve on prior fMRI-based ADHD classifiers' speed and accuracy.

emb:L2005444671.model_family: neural network; compared against a rule-based Sliding Window Method algorithm
emb:L2005444671.clinical_problem: objective measurement of scoliosis curve severity (Cobb angle) in idiopathic scoliosis
emb:L2005444671.patient_population: 300 digital spine X-rays from children with idiopathic scoliosis
emb:L2005444671.model_description: The study trains algorithms to identify the vertebral column and individual vertebrae on spine X-rays and construct the tangent lines needed to compute the Cobb angle in children with idiopathic scoliosis. A dataset of 300 X-rays, manually measured by a radiologist as ground truth, was used to train and validate a neural network, and a rule-based Sliding Window Method was also tested and found superior to the machine-learning approach in this preliminary work.
emb:L2005444671.dataset_size: 300 digital spine X-rays of children with idiopathic scoliosis
emb:L2005444671.headline_result: Achieved greater than 85% training accuracy for Cobb angle determination

emb:L2007399413.clinical_problem: detection of fetal hydrocephalus on prenatal ultrasound
emb:L2007399413.patient_population: fetuses (approximately 20-22 weeks gestation) undergoing head ultrasound
emb:L2007399413.model_description: A convolutional neural network classifies fetal head ultrasound images as hydrocephalic or healthy, aiming to automate what is normally a manual biometric assessment of morphological malformation detectable around 20-22 weeks of gestation. The CNN-based method achieved high classification performance and is proposed to assess anomalous cases with reduced processing time compared to prior work.

emb:L2008007488.exclusion_reason: erratum/correction notice, not a research paper

emb:L635109110.exclusion_reason: gestational age estimation from newborn blood metabolomic markers, not imaging-based

emb:L2004846904.patient_population: 148 children and adolescents aged 2-17 years in Guizhou, left hand-wrist radiographs
emb:L2004846904.model_description: A deep-learning bone-age assessment model, trained on the CH 05 RUS-CHN standard, estimates bone age from left hand-wrist radiographs of children and adolescents in Guizhou. Its estimates were compared with a reference standard set by three experts and with estimates from two resident doctors, evaluating error and the proportion of readings within one year of the reference.
emb:L2004846904.headline_result: Model MAE 0.295 years (95% CI 0.238-0.352), 93.92% within 1 year of reference; model outperformed one resident doctor (MAE 0.438 years, P=0.002) but not the other (MAE 0.360 years, P=0.120)

emb:L2004846905.model_family: AI bone-age assessment system (method not further specified)
emb:L2004846905.patient_population: 130 hand-wrist radiographs of children aged 1-13 years
emb:L2004846905.model_description: An artificial-intelligence system estimates carpal bone age and carpal maturity scores from hand-wrist radiographs of children aged 1-13 years, compared against three senior radiologists' reference standard and three junior radiologists' independent readings, evaluating agreement and reading time.
emb:L2004846905.dataset_size: 130 hand-wrist radiographs of children aged 1-13 years
emb:L2004846905.headline_result: ICC between AI system and reference standard 0.997 (vs 0.994-0.997 for junior radiologists); AI reading time significantly shorter than physicians' (all P<0.05)

emb:L2004846920.exclusion_reason: adult hepatitis B cirrhosis population (Child-Pugh grading), no pediatric patients

emb:L2004174435.model_family: deep learning model (China 05 RUS-CHN bone age standard)
emb:L2004174435.patient_population: 5,000 children with suspected metabolic disorders from Wuxi Children's Hospital; 2,351 in training set and 101 in validation set
emb:L2004174435.model_description: A deep-learning bone-age assessment model was built on the China 05 RUS-CHN standard using left-hand radiographs from 5,000 children with suspected metabolic disorders at Wuxi Children's Hospital, with four pediatric radiologists' averaged double-blind readings as the reference standard. In a preliminary clinical validation, the model's accuracy, mean absolute error, and time efficiency were compared against two resident doctors on a held-out validation set.
emb:L2004174435.headline_result: MAE 0.37±0.35 years, RMSE 0.50 years vs reference standard; accuracy 94.1% within ±1.0 year, 89.1% within ±0.7 year, 74.3% within ±0.5 year; no significant difference from two resident doctors (P>0.05)

emb:L630195533.model_family: BiSeNet (spatial path + context path fusion CNN)
emb:L630195533.clinical_problem: segmentation of cardiac structures on pediatric echocardiography for biometric measurement and diagnosis
emb:L630195533.patient_population: 87 pediatric echocardiography videos (2,216 images) from Shenzhen Children's Hospital
emb:L630195533.model_description: BiSeNet, a convolutional network combining a spatial path and a context path via feature fusion, segments the left ventricle and left atrium on pediatric echocardiography images, replacing time-consuming manual sonographer segmentation. It was trained and evaluated on 87 echocardiography videos (2,216 images) from Shenzhen Children's Hospital against sonographers' manual ground truth.
emb:L630195533.dataset_size: 87 echocardiography videos (2,216 images) from Shenzhen Children's Hospital

emb:L2004162615.model_family: regression convolutional neural network with extreme gradient boosting decision tree
emb:L2004162615.clinical_problem: bone age estimation from characteristic regions of interest on hand radiographs
emb:L2004162615.patient_population: 11,858 children aged 0-18 years at Children's Hospital of Shanghai (training/validation), plus a separate 1,229-subject test set
emb:L2004162615.model_description: An improved regression convolutional neural network combined with an extreme gradient boosting decision tree first detects traditional regions of interest on hand radiographs, then predicts bone age from features in those regions. Trained on 80% and validated on 20% of 11,858 hand radiographs from children aged 0-18 at the Children's Hospital of Shanghai, and separately tested on 1,229 additional subjects, comparing its predictions against pediatric radiologists.
emb:L2004162615.dataset_size: 11,858 subjects (training/validation) plus 1,229-subject test set, children aged 0-18 years
emb:L2004162615.headline_result: Region-detection mAP 0.91; MAE 0.461 years (male) and 0.431 years (female); 90.07% of test predictions within 1 year of radiologists' assessment, accuracy 96.67%

emb:L2001971587.exclusion_reason: EEG-based brain-network classification, not radiologic imaging

emb:L2002525362.model_family: 3D densely connected convolutional network (DenseNet) with skip connections
emb:L2002525362.clinical_problem: segmentation of 6-month-old infant brain tissue (white matter, gray matter, CSF)
emb:L2002525362.model_description: 3D-SkipDenseSeg is a fully convolutional densely connected network with skip connections that segments 6-month-old infant brain MRI into white matter, gray matter, and cerebrospinal fluid, addressing the low tissue contrast typical at this age. Evaluated on the public iSeg-2017 dataset, it achieved the best Dice similarity coefficients among 21 participating challenge teams while using only 10-30% of the parameters of comparable deep-learning methods.
emb:L2002525362.dataset_size: iSeg-2017 public 6-month infant brain MRI dataset
emb:L2002525362.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 90.37±1.38% (WM), 92.27±0.81% (GM), 95.79±0.54% (CSF); best among 21 participating iSeg-2017 teams

emb:L2002789931.exclusion_reason: feasibility study spans mostly non-radiologic imaging (retinal fundus, OCT, dermoscopy) with only one of five datasets being mixed pediatric/adult chest X-ray, not focused on pediatric radiology
